chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal narrated from Muhammad ibn Ali, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Yahya ibn Abd Allah ibn Hasan, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Divorce is not valid under compulsion, nor is manumission (freeing a slave) valid under compulsion, nor is an oath valid for severing ties of kinship, nor for anything from disobedience to Allah. So whoever swore or was made to swear regarding any of this, or did it, there is nothing upon him (it is not binding).'

And he said: 'Divorce is only that which is intended by divorce, without compulsion and without harm to the waiting period, or according to the Sunnah on a period of purity without sexual intercourse, and with two witnesses. So whoever contradicts this, his divorce and his oath are not anything that is referred back to the Book of Allah, Exalted and Mighty.'
ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for a valid divorce in Shia jurisprudence according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that divorce, manumission, and oaths are invalid if performed under compulsion or for severing kinship ties, emphasizing that true divorce requires specific intention and adherence to the Sunnah of purity without intercourse. He further stipulates the necessity of two witnesses, noting that deviation from these conditions renders the act not binding according to the Quran. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential focus on the interplay between internal intent (niyyah) and external form (sighah) in validating personal status acts.
